nominal.note: The signal-lamp color for 'still live, working as expected' states: the header LIVE pulse dot, the MITIGATED status tag, and the default focus ring. Never used for OPEN or alarm states.

amber.note: The third rung of the status traffic light, spent on exactly one job: the OPEN status tag and its pulse dot. Distinct from both Nominal (stable/monitored) and Alarm (needs a human now).

alarm.note: Reserved for genuine, blocking alarm states rendered as a solid fill: an expired mitigation and a version-conflict notice. Never used for a routine status.

alarm-muted.note: Same alarm meaning at inline, non-blocking volume: form validation errors, a failed directory load, a session-expired notice, the feed's own WIRE DOWN state. Always a bordered text-only treatment, never a solid fill.

alarm-ink.note: Text/border color placed on top of an Alarm Red fill; also the inverse color on an alarm control's hover/focus state.

paper-raised.note: The background behind both slide-over panels (incident detail, new-incident form) — a lighter paper tone than the page ground beneath it.

steel.note: Reserved for the masthead's double-rule border only. Repeated identically on the wire desk, login screen, and admin directory headers.

rule.note: The hairline divider between bulletins, and the border around every button, chip, segmented control, and input field.

display.purpose: Orbitron. Used only for the "POSTMORTEM" nameplate, repeated on the wire desk, login screen, and admin directory headers.

title.purpose: Chakra Petch. An incident's own title (bulletin row + detail panel) and a slide-over panel's own heading (e.g. "FILE NEW INCIDENT").

body.purpose: JetBrains Mono. Meta lines: reporter, elapsed time, mitigation summary, form help text.

label.purpose: JetBrains Mono, tracked-out uppercase. Status tags, precedence stamps, buttons, form-field labels, role toggle, LIVE indicator, and ALL CLEAR / WIRE DOWN state headings.

motion.name: feed-container
motion.purpose: The parent stagger driving the feed, both slide-over panels' section reveal, and the admin directory list. One shared entrance choreography, not per-surface animation.

motion.name: feed-item-spring
motion.value: opacity 0→1, y 16px→0, type: spring, stiffness: 120, damping: 20
motion.purpose: Each child's own rise-and-settle within the shared stagger. Plays once per mount; a feed re-sort after claim/resolve doesn't replay it.

motion.name: panel-slide
motion.value: transform translate, 300ms, bottom-docked on mobile / right-docked at sm+
motion.purpose: The incident detail panel and new-incident form's own entrance/exit, independent of the content stagger inside them.

motion.name: pulse-ping
motion.purpose: The live-status dot's expanding ring, on the header LIVE indicator and an OPEN/MITIGATED status tag.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Wraps the whole desk; disengages the stagger/spring/slide choreography automatically for users with reduced-motion preferences set.

components.name: Wire Header
components.description: The single persistent masthead, repeated identically on the wire desk, login screen, and admin directory: nameplate (Orbitron), subtitle, and (on the wire desk) a live heartbeat cluster plus the signed-in user's name/role and an admin-only 'MANAGE USERS' link.
components.html:
POSTMORTEM

INCIDENT WIRE

LIVE15:53:05Z
components.css: @keyframes ds-ping { 75%, 100% { transform: scale(2); opacity: 0; } } .ds-wire-header { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; padding: 16px 20px; border-bottom: 4px double var(--color-steel); font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; } .ds-wire-header__nameplate { margin: 0; font-family: 'Orbitron', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 800; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-wire-header__subtitle { margin: 2px 0 0; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.2em; color: var(--color-ink-dim); } .ds-wire-header__live { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding-bottom: 2px; } .ds-wire-header__live-label { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.15em; color: var(--color-nominal); } .ds-wire-header__clock { font-size: 14px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--color-ink-dim); } .ds-pulse-dot { position: relative; display: inline-flex; height: 8px; width: 8px; } .ds-pulse-dot__ping { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-nominal); opacity: 0.6; animation: ds-ping 1.5s cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1) infinite; } .ds-pulse-dot__core { position: relative; height: 8px; width: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-nominal); }

components.name: Precedence Stamp
components.description: Severity read through typography alone — weight, size, and tracking escalate from ROUTINE to FLASH. Never color. Set in JetBrains Mono, not a display face.
components.css: .ds-precedence { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-precedence--flash { font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-precedence--urgent { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-precedence--bulletin { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-precedence--routine { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--color-ink-dim); }

components.name: Status Tag
components.description: The three-way status traffic light: OPEN pulses in Amber, MITIGATED pulses in Nominal Green, RESOLVED sits flat in Faded Wire Ink with no dot.
components.html: OPEN
components.css: @keyframes ds-ping { 75%, 100% { transform: scale(2); opacity: 0; } } .ds-status-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; } .ds-status-tag--open { color: var(--color-amber); } .ds-status-tag--mitigated { color: var(--color-nominal); } .ds-status-tag--resolved { color: var(--color-ink-dim); } .ds-pulse-dot--sm { height: 6px; width: 6px; } .ds-pulse-dot--sm .ds-pulse-dot__ping, .ds-pulse-dot--sm .ds-pulse-dot__core { height: 6px; width: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-amber); } .ds-pulse-dot--sm .ds-pulse-dot__ping { position: absolute; inset: 0; opacity: 0.6; animation: ds-ping 1.5s cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1) infinite; } .ds-pulse-dot--sm .ds-pulse-dot__core { position: relative; }

components.name: Incident Bulletin
components.description: The feed row itself: no card shell, just a hairline bottom border, full-bleed against the page. Title is set in Chakra Petch; everything else stays in JetBrains Mono. Hovers to a flat tint, never a shadow.
components.html:
URGENT14:58Zauth-service

Elevated login latency after cert rotation

REPORTED BY T. ÁLVAREZ · 54M AGO
components.css: .ds-bulletin { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-rule); padding: 16px 20px; transition: background-color 0.15s; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; } .ds-bulletin:hover { background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-paper-dim) 60%, transparent); } .ds-bulletin__top { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 12px; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-bulletin__meta { font-size: 12px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--color-ink-dim); } .ds-bulletin__title { margin: 4px 0 8px; font-family: 'Chakra Petch', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 20px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--color-ink); }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: One bordered, divided strip reused across three unrelated surfaces: the new-incident severity picker, the admin role toggle, and the login screen's sign-in/register tabs. Active segment inverts to Wire Ink fill.
components.css: .ds-segmented { display: flex; border: 1px solid var(--color-rule); } .ds-segmented__item { min-height: 44px; flex: 1; padding: 0 12px; border-left: 1px solid var(--color-rule); font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--color-ink-dim); background: transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-segmented__item:first-child { border-left: none; } .ds-segmented__item:hover { color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-segmented__item--active, .ds-segmented__item--active:hover { background: var(--color-ink); color: var(--color-paper); }

components.name: Mitigation Readout — Expired
components.description: The alarm state: a solid Alarm Red fill, one of two places the reserved blocking-alarm signal is spent (the other being the version-conflict notice).
components.css: .ds-mitigation-expired { display: flex; align-items: center; border: 1px solid var(--color-alarm); background: var(--color-alarm); padding: 6px 10px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--color-alarm-ink); }

components.name: Conflict Notice
components.description: Blocking alarm-state notice for a detected concurrent edit (optimistic-locking version conflict) in the incident detail panel — the same solid Alarm Red pattern as the expired mitigation. It replaces the panel's action row entirely until reloaded.
components.html: CONFLICT: incident was updated by another request. Expected version 4, but current version is 5.
components.css: .ds-conflict { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--color-alarm); background: var(--color-alarm); padding: 12px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; } .ds-conflict__message { margin: 0; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.02em; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--color-alarm-ink); } .ds-conflict__reload { display: inline-flex; align-self: flex-start; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; border: 1px solid var(--color-alarm-ink); background: transparent; padding: 0 16px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; color: var(--color-alarm-ink); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-conflict__reload:hover, .ds-conflict__reload:focus-visible { background: var(--color-alarm-ink); color: var(--color-alarm); }

components.name: Claim Control — Unclaimed / Claimed
components.description: The primary action: outlined at rest, fully inverts fill/text on hover and focus alike. Once claimed, it becomes a static stamp, not a toggle — ownership as a permanent mark, matching the audit trail's append-only discipline.
components.css: .ds-claim-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 16px; border: 1px solid var(--color-ink); background: transparent; color: var(--color-ink); font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-claim-btn:hover, .ds-claim-btn:focus-visible { background: var(--color-ink); color: var(--color-paper); } .ds-claimed-stamp { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border: 1px solid var(--color-rule); padding: 4px 8px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: var(--color-ink-dim); }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: The shared field style behind the new-incident form and both auth forms: always-visible tracked-out label above a bordered, transparent-background input at the 44px touch-target floor.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; } .ds-field__label { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; color: var(--color-ink-dim); } .ds-field__input { min-height: 44px; width: 100%; border: 1px solid var(--color-rule); background: transparent; padding: 0 12px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 14px; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-field__input::placeholder { color: var(--color-ink-dim); } .ds-field__input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-nominal); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Empty / Error State Heading
components.description: The feed's two terminal states: ALL CLEAR (Nominal Green, bold) when there are no incidents, WIRE DOWN (Alarm Muted, bold — quiet, non-blocking volume) on a load failure. Both are JetBrains Mono labels, not a display face.
components.css: .ds-state-heading { margin: 0; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; } .ds-state-heading--nominal { color: var(--color-nominal); } .ds-state-heading--alarm { color: var(--color-alarm-muted); }

narrative.overview:
PostMortem's dashboard is not a status-card grid — it's a continuous wire feed, the same discipline a newsroom telex applies to incoming copy: timestamped, precedence-graded, append-only, never silently edited. This is a deliberate refusal of the generic-SaaS dashboard default (colored status pills in a card grid); the system's own thesis is that the audit-trail discipline the product is built on — nothing is silently overwritten, every action punches a new line — deserves a visual form that behaves the same way. The page reads top-down like dispatch copy, most urgent and most recent first, not as a dashboard the eye has to hunt across.

The palette is near-monochrome by design: warm manila paper and dark ink by day, gunmetal ground and amber ink by night — the same machine under a different light source, not an inverted theme. Against that neutral field sit two reserved signal-lamp colors, nominal green and alarm red, plus a third traffic-light rung, amber, spent on exactly one job: the OPEN status. Nominal green means "still live, working as expected." Alarm red — as a solid fill — means "this needs a human now," and its quieter cousin, alarm-muted, carries the same meaning at a lower volume for inline error text and non-blocking load failures. Severity itself never touches color at all — FLASH/URGENT/BULLETIN/ROUTINE is a typographic ladder of weight and size, the wire service's own precedence vocabulary. The desk gained a second typographic voice since its first cut: Orbitron for the masthead nameplate alone, and Chakra Petch reserved for an incident's own title and the two slide-over panels that carry one. Everything else — status, meta lines, the audit trail, every form field, every button label — still runs in JetBrains Mono, the machine's own instrumentation face. Every surface is flat: no shadows, no rounded corners anywhere except the two functional live-pulse dots. New surfaces (the incident detail panel, the new-incident form, the admin user directory) mount with a shared, quiet spring stagger rather than snapping into place, but the system stays otherwise as restrained as it always was: nothing decorative, nothing added for warmth that isn't earned by function.
keyCharacteristics: Continuous append-only feed, not a card grid — one bulletin per incident, dividers not gutters.
Near-monochrome manila/gunmetal palette with a three-color status ladder (amber/nominal/dim) and two reserved alarm colors (full-fill alarm, quieter alarm-muted) that never do routine-status duty.
Severity communicated by typography (weight, size, tracking), never by color.
Two typographic voices, both rare: Orbitron for the masthead only, Chakra Petch for incident titles and panel headings only. Everything else is JetBrains Mono.
Zero shadows, zero border-radius except the two functional pulse dots.
Day desk / night desk: light and dark are two lighting conditions on one machine, not an inversion.
New panels and lists mount with a shared staggered-spring entrance; the choreography is a system rule, not a one-off flourish.

rules.name: The Reserved-Signal Rule
rules.body: Amber, Nominal, and Alarm each mean exactly one thing and never trade places: Amber is "open, needs action." Nominal is "live and working as expected." Alarm (full fill) is "needs a human right now"; Alarm Muted is the same meaning at inline, non-blocking volume.

rules.name: The Day Desk / Night Desk Rule
rules.body: Light and dark mode are not an inverted palette — they're two lighting conditions on the same machine (prefers-color-scheme, not a manual toggle). Every neutral and every signal color gets an explicit day value and an explicit night value; neither is derived by inverting the other.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Orbitron is spent on exactly one element: the masthead nameplate. Chakra Petch is spent on exactly two: an incident's title and a slide-over panel's own heading. Every other element runs in JetBrains Mono.

rules.name: The Precedence-By-Weight Rule
rules.body: Severity is FLASH / URGENT / BULLETIN / ROUTINE — words, never a color chip — and each step down the ladder loses weight, size, and tracking in the same motion. A reader triages by glancing at type density alone.

rules.name: The Flat Wire Rule
rules.body: No shadow, ever. If something needs to feel more important, it gets a heavier border, a lighter/raised paper tone, or one of the reserved signal colors — never a drop shadow pretending the screen has depth it doesn't.

rules.name: The Right-Angle Rule
rules.body: Radius is reserved for exactly one thing: the circular pulse indicator that means "this is live." Every other shape in the system is a hard rectangle.

rules.name: The One-Entrance Rule
rules.body: Every data-bearing surface that mounts — the feed, a slide-over panel, the admin directory — uses the same stagger-and-spring choreography, never a bespoke animation per surface.

dos: Do keep Amber, Nominal, and Alarm each meaning exactly one thing — OPEN, "live and working," and "needs a human now," respectively.
Do communicate severity through the weight/size/tracking ladder (FLASH → ROUTINE), never through a color chip.
Do give every color token an explicit day value and an explicit night value tied to prefers-color-scheme — never derive dark mode by inverting light mode.
Do keep every rectangular surface at 0 radius; the only permitted curve is the functional live-pulse dot.
Do limit Orbitron to the masthead nameplate and Chakra Petch to incident titles and panel headings; everything else runs in JetBrains Mono.
Do reuse the bordered segmented-control pattern (severity picker, role toggle, auth tabs) rather than inventing a new selector style per form.
Do use the shared stagger-and-spring entrance for any new data-bearing surface, and respect reducedMotion="user" rather than hardcoding animation.
Do set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on any live-updating numeral — clocks, countdowns, elapsed-time strings — so digits never jitter the layout.
Do keep interactive targets at a minimum 44px height, per the product's ICU-grade accessibility commitment.
donts: Don't use Amber, Nominal Green, and Alarm Red interchangeably, or introduce a further general-purpose accent — the palette's force comes from each hue meaning exactly one thing.
Don't give a form field a colored border to signal an error; errors are their own text-only Alarm Muted line, never a recolored input.
Don't add box-shadow or simulated elevation anywhere; depth is stroke weight, tint delta, and (for panels) a lighter paper tone — never a shadow.
Don't round a button, card, divider, or form field; radius is spent entirely on the pulse-dot indicators.
Don't spread either display typeface beyond its one reserved job — Orbitron is not a general headline face, and Chakra Petch is not a body or label face.
Don't turn "claimed" into a toggle a responder can undo casually — claiming is a stamp, a one-way mark, matching the audit trail's append-only discipline.
